agyos_skill.intent: Design user flows and screen structure using StyleSeed UX patterns such as progressive disclosure, hub-and-spoke navigation, and information pyramids.
agyos_skill.instructions: Part of [StyleSeed](https://github.com/bitjaru/styleseed), this skill designs flows before screens. It uses proven UX patterns to define entry points, exits, screen inventory, and navigation structure so the implementation has a coherent user journey instead of a pile of disconnected pages. - Use when planning onboarding, checkout, account management, dashboards, or drill-down flows - Use when a new feature spans multiple screens or modal states - Use when users need a clear path through a task instead of a single isolated page - Use when the UI needs navigation logic before components are built - progressive disclosure: reveal complexity only when needed - Miller's Law: chunk content into manageable groups - Hick's Law: minimize decision overload on each screen - hub and spoke for dashboards and detail views - linear flow for onboarding, forms, and checkout - tab navigation for 3 to 5 top-level areas - every flow has a clear entry point - every flow has a clear exit or success condition - key features should usually be reachable within three taps from home - non-root screens need back navigation - loading, empty, and error states need explicit recovery paths Provide: 1. An ASCII flow diagram 2. A screen inventory with each screen's purpose 3. Edge cases for loading, empty, and error states 4. Recommended page scaffolds and reusable patterns to implement next - Optimize for clarity before density - Let one screen answer one primary question - Keep escape hatches visible for risky or destructive steps - Define state transitions before drawing detailed layouts
